title: Ergonomic stream orchestration with idempotent replay
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
Deliver a developer-friendly Python SDK surface for streaming chat completions that treats the stream as an explicit, iterable session with ergonomic event dispatch and an idempotent replay mechanism. The goal is to make common patterns (partial responses, tool calls, metadata events, reconnects) simple and safe for application code without leaking low-level transport details.

Motivation and scope:
- Customers report complexity wiring up SSE/websocket streams, handling mid-stream tool call events, and replaying partial transcripts after network blips.
- Current internal examples require stitching multiple primitives; we want a single, well-documented pattern that covers: graceful resume, deterministic replay, soft-commit checkpoints, telemetry hooks, and a small sync/async ergonomic façade.
- Target audience: Python SDK users building chat UIs, server-side assistants, and serverless functions that need reliable streaming semantics.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Session abstraction: StreamSession(context_id, model, metadata) returned by client.chat.stream(). Exposes:
   - async iterator over EventEnvelope objects (event_type, payload, seq, replay_token)
   - .checkpoint() method that yields a short-lived idempotency token (soft-commit)
   - .replay(replay_token) to rehydrate state from any checkpointed point (idempotent replay)
2) EventEnvelope model: small, typed envelope with stable sequence numbers, event semantic (message.delta, message.final, tool.call, tool.result, meta.alert). Intentionally minimal to avoid heavy SDK model types.
3) Telemetry hooks: event-level and session-level callbacks for metrics, with lightweight sampling by default.
4) Backpressure and flow control: an optional bounded buffer parameter and a sync wrapper using a thread-safe iterator for sync consumers.
5) Retry semantics: automatic soft-reconnect for transient transport failures (exponential backoff with jitter) up to configurable attempts; permanent failures expose an error event. Replay uses replay_token and server-side resume point matching.

Trade-offs considered:
- We considered a richer typed event hierarchy (separate classes per event), but chose a compact envelope to keep stability across model changes and to reduce cognitive burden for end users.
- We debated full transactional commit semantics vs. soft checkpoints. Full transactional commits would require heavier server work and client blocking. Soft checkpoints provide a usable, light-weight compromise for most app patterns.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDK surface documented in SDK docs page and example notebook.
- Integration test coverage: simulated SSE disconnect + replay path passes deterministic transcript assert.
- Demo app (chat UI) updated and manual smoke-tested for reconnect and replay UX.
- Telemetry hooks emit event counts and replay-rate metric to the streaming dashboard.
- No user-facing API churn in the next minor release; API is behind a feature flag for a 2-week dogfood period.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (spike + spec): implement prototype in a branch that returns Session + envelope iterator, basic replay token plumbing. (Done)
- Phase 2 (core): add checkpoint API, replay API, and server-side resume integration; unit tests for sequence monotonicity and idempotency. (In progress)
- Phase 3 (ergonomics): add sync wrapper, context manager support, and convenience helpers (emit_tool_calls, collect_partial_text). Add docs and examples. (Next)
- Phase 4 (rollout): feature-flagged beta, dogfood with internal teams, iterate on API based on feedback, then flip flag.

Links to artifacts:
- Proposal: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SDK/pages/stream-orchestration-proposal
- Design notes (internal notebook): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_stream_design_mockup
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/4821
- Dashboard (telemetry): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/streaming-latency?range=7d

Open questions / risks:
- Server-side resume semantics need a clear consistency contract (what happens to tool calls that were in-flight). We plan to mark tool.call events as idempotent by generating server replay IDs.
- Memory/cost: checkpointing frequency trades off between granularity and server storage. Default checkpoint interval will be conservative (every 8s or on explicit .checkpoint()).
- UX: should .checkpoint() be implicit on final message? Decided: yes, final messages auto-checkpoint; explicit calls still allowed for mid-stream safe points.

Next steps for this ticket:
- Complete unit tests for replay edge-cases and sequence gaps (Marcus).
- Add sync iterator wrapper and context manager (Marcus).
- Draft SDK docs + example notebook for the repo (Aisha).
- Schedule dogfood invites with Console and Solutions (PM).
acceptance_criteria: Session abstraction exposed in Python client (async iterator + checkpoint/replay API)
Integration test: SSE disconnect -> .replay(replay_token) -> exact transcript match
Sync wrapper and context manager available for sync-only apps
Docs and example notebook published under sdk-python streaming docs
Telemetry emits replay_rate and session_error_count to streaming dashboard
